ideas.title: Signed Waivers for Zeffy Event Tickets

notes.stateful: The organiser keeps a signed, dated record per event and per ticket, with the waiver version each signer saw, and comes back to it for every event and season.
notes.connected: Connects to the organisation's Zeffy account with its own API key and receives Zeffy's signed payment.completed webhook, which carries each ticket's attendee and per-ticket answers.
notes.unattended: A webhook sends each new ticket's guardian a signing link, and a scheduled job chases unsigned tickets before the event date.
notes.shared: The organiser writes the waiver, a parent or adult attendee signs it, and door staff work from the check-in list.

buildPlan.title: One event, one signature
buildPlan.delivers: An organiser signs in, pastes a waiver, connects a Zeffy key, and a test ticket's buyer receives a signing link and signs; the signed PDF is stored.
buildPlan.acceptance: A seeded payment.completed webhook with a valid Zeffy-Signature header creates one signing request; the signed record holds the signer, time, waiver text hash and ticket id; deployed.

buildPlan.title: Per-ticket attendees and guardians
buildPlan.delivers: Each ticket on a multi-ticket order gets its own record; a parent signs once per child named on the tickets.
buildPlan.acceptance: A webhook with three tickets yields three records linked to three attendee contact ids; signing one does not mark the others signed.

buildPlan.title: Waiver versions and audit trail
buildPlan.delivers: The organiser edits the waiver per event; each signature keeps the exact version, a hash, the time and the signer's typed or drawn signature, and a PDF copy is emailed to the signer.
buildPlan.acceptance: Changing the text after a signature leaves the old record unchanged and verifiable by hash; the emailed PDF matches the stored one byte for byte.

buildPlan.title: Chasing the unsigned
buildPlan.delivers: A scheduled job reminds unsigned ticket holders 7, 3 and 1 days before the event and stops when they sign.
buildPlan.acceptance: With a seeded event in 7 days and two unsigned tickets, exactly two reminders go out per scheduled step and none after signing.

buildPlan.title: Door list
buildPlan.delivers: A phone-friendly check-in page per event lists every ticket, signed or not, with the photo-consent answer from Zeffy's own per-ticket question.
buildPlan.acceptance: The page loads 200 tickets in under 2 seconds on a throttled connection and filters to unsigned in one tap; staff access is by a per-event link that can be revoked.

buildPlan.title: Polish
buildPlan.delivers: Organiser README, retention setting per event, export of all signed PDFs as one zip, keyboard and screen-reader pass, walkthrough test.
buildPlan.acceptance: A walkthrough test runs sign-in to door list; axe reports no serious issues; the zip contains one PDF per signed ticket.

Then, on the day, you cannot tell which children are covered and which are not.

benefits: A signed, dated waiver for each child or adult attending
Reminders go out on their own until everyone has signed

ideas.problemStatement: Organisers who sell event and camp tickets through Zeffy need a liability waiver signed and dated for every attendee, adults and children; Zeffy offers only a required checkbox or a file on the thank-you email, so organisers bolt on outside forms that are not tied to the tickets and cannot tell on the day who has signed.
ideas.description: The organiser connects their Zeffy organisation with its API key and turns on Zeffy's payment.completed webhook. When a ticket is bought, the service creates one record per ticket from the attendee data Zeffy sends and emails the buyer a signing link for each attendee. The signer reads the organiser's waiver for that event and signs by typing or drawing; the record keeps the waiver version, a hash, the time and a PDF copy, which is also emailed to the signer. A scheduled job chases unsigned tickets before the event, and door staff open a phone-friendly list showing who has signed, alongside the photo-consent answer Zeffy already collects per ticket.
ideas.targetCustomer: Volunteer organisers and administrators of small nonprofits, summer camps, youth programmes, clubs and parent groups that sell event or camp tickets on Zeffy.
ideas.buyer: The organisation, from its operating or event budget; seasonal events suggest a per-event or per-signature price rather than a subscription.
ideas.whyNow: Zeffy has added ticketing and check-in features every month in 2026 (group check-in 2026-09-28, volunteer check-in access 2026-10-13, family memberships 2026-10-16, check-in badges 2026-11-17) but nothing for waivers or signatures, while requests for them kept coming through 2026-10 and 2026-11; its public API now exposes per-ticket attendees and signed webhooks.

ideas.techStack: React + Vite front end, Supabase for sign-in and per-app data, a webhook receiver and PDF rendering on backend-hub (Render), the platform's transactional email and scheduled jobs.

pricing.model: Per signed participant, or a season pass per organisation
pricing.pricePoint: $1 per signed participant, or $29 per season
pricing.rationale: Organisers chose Zeffy because it is free and run seasonal events, so a monthly fee invites sign-up-and-cancel; WaiverSign charges $19 a month for 100 waivers and esigned $9 a month plus a fee per signature.

ideas.revenueSketch: Estimate: 150 organisations a season collecting 120 signatures each at $1 = $18,000 a season; the number of organisations is an assumption, not a measured figure.
ideas.distribution: First 10: search for Zeffy waiver queries ('zeffy waiver', 'zeffy permission slip'), where Zeffy's own help article admits the gap, and a listing request to Zeffy's Experts directory (https://www.zeffy.com/en-gb/home/experts), which today lists consultants and agencies, not apps, through an external application form; rule unknown: check before applying. Zeffy's community guidelines say 'Off-topic promotion or spam doesn't belong here.' (https://community.zeffy.com/community-guidelines): not a channel. Never post on Zeffy's feature board, which holds the evidence.

validationTest.method: A one-page site, 'Signed waivers for your Zeffy event tickets (not affiliated with Zeffy)', with an example door list and a '$1 per signed participant, reserve a place' button leading to a waitlist; a 21-day search-ad test on phrase and exact matches for Zeffy waiver queries; no outreach and no posts in the evidence threads.
validationTest.successCriteria: At least 5 waitlist sign-ups and 8 price-button clicks from Zeffy organisers in 21 days; fewer than 300 ad impressions in 21 days means search is too thin a channel.
validationTest.cost: About $150 in ads, a domain and one build day.

ideas.moat: Thin: a tie to one host's ticket data and a store of signed records that organisers do not want to move; Zeffy could build the same feature.
compliance: E-signature (US ESIGN Act and UETA): keep consent, intent, the signer, the time and the exact waiver text, and give the signer a copy.
COPPA: a parent fills in the form; the FTC says COPPA does not cover information collected from adults that may pertain to children (FAQ F.4). Children never sign.
Minors' waivers: enforceability varies by US state; the product must not promise that a waiver holds, and organisers supply their own text.
Retention: minors' waivers may need keeping for years (one university policy keeps them three years or until age 20), so retention and export must outlive a season.
GDPR and UK GDPR: for organisations in the UK and Ireland the product is a processor and needs a data-processing agreement.
Security: the Zeffy key is owner-created, covers the whole organisation and can write and delete data; store it encrypted and use it read-only.

risks.risk: Zeffy ships waivers or file questions itself.
risks.mitigation: Keep the build small, price per event, and stop if Zeffy announces it.

risks.risk: Organisers on a free platform will not pay.
risks.mitigation: Price per signed participant so an organiser pays only when it has an event.

risks.risk: Door staff work from two lists, Zeffy's check-in and this one.
risks.mitigation: Make the door list a filter of unsigned tickets only, so it complements Zeffy's check-in.

risks.risk: A long-lived store of minors' signed records.
risks.mitigation: Per-event retention settings, export, and deletion at the organiser's request.

scoreRationale.pain: Requests across two posts with 52 and 41 votes, one dated 2026-10-16 (https://feedback.zeffy.com/feature-requests/p/digital-waiver-integration-for-school-events); held at 3 because Zeffy's free required per-ticket question gives a checkbox acknowledgement (https://support.zeffy.com/how-can-i-ask-my-donors-custom-questions).
scoreRationale.willingnessToPay: One paid app for the same job on another platform (https://apps.shopify.com/esigned) and paid waiver plans (https://waiversign.com/digital-waiver-pricing); one organiser says they would pay for an add-on (https://feedback.zeffy.com/feature-requests/p/waivers-1); no paid job found.
scoreRationale.reachability: Self-serve search on Zeffy waiver queries only; Zeffy has no app marketplace, its Experts directory lists consultants (https://www.zeffy.com/en-gb/home/experts) and its community bans promotion (https://community.zeffy.com/community-guidelines).
scoreRationale.competitiveGap: No waiver tool tied to Zeffy tickets was found, but Zeffy's free per-ticket questions cover consent answers (https://support.zeffy.com/how-can-i-ask-my-donors-custom-questions) and SignUpGenius signs free if checkout moves (https://www.signupgenius.com/forms-and-waivers).
scoreRationale.feasibility: Zeffy's API gives per-ticket attendees and answers with HMAC-signed webhooks (https://www.zeffy.com/api/docs); it cannot write to Zeffy's check-in app, so the door list is separate.
scoreRationale.complianceBurden: Long-lived minors' signed records and an organisation-wide API key (https://www.westernu.edu/legal/risk-management/waivers-of-liability-and-release-agreements, https://www.zeffy.com/api/docs).

review.findings: A watchlist entry first seen 2026-11-21 at 19, re-researched today. Research kept it at 18 and re-scoped it to ticketed events: Zeffy shipped nothing for waivers, signatures or attachments from August to November 2026, the API gives per-ticket attendees and answers with signed webhooks, and no free tool ties signatures to Zeffy tickets. The adversarial reviewer cut it to 16: competitiveGap 3 to 2, because Zeffy's free required per-attendee questions already give photo consent and a per-child acknowledgement printed on each e-ticket, and complianceBurden 3 to 2, for years of minors' signed records and an organisation-wide key that can delete data. It found poster E's request was about vendors reading policies, not attendee waivers, that the youth programme's permission-slip link was a working workaround, and that waivers are far from the top of Zeffy's board. Re-scoped to guardian-signed waiver PDFs matched to each ticket, with reminders and a door list, priced per signature.

missing: pain 3 is below 4: Zeffy's free per-ticket checkbox is an accepted workaround for some organisers
gateGap.closedBy: The waitlist and search-ad test: 5 sign-ups and 8 price clicks at $1 per signed participant would confirm willingness to pay; dated complaints that an insurer, a lawyer or a school board rejected the checkbox would lift pain to 4.

ideas.title: Volunteer Match Schedules for Grants

notes.stateful: The organisation keeps its awards, role rates with their documented basis, imported hour entries, allocations and an audit log, and returns every month.
notes.connected: Imports the approved-hours CSV the organisation already exports from POINT (Hours Start Time, Contact, Hours Duration, Program, Status), Golden, SignUpGenius or a sheet.
notes.unattended: A scheduled job emails the program manager before each award's invoice date, listing approved hours not yet allocated and awards short of their match.
notes.engine: Values each entry from a role rate table with its basis (2 CFR 200.306(e)), locks each entry to exactly one award (200.306(b)(2)) and enforces caps per award period.
notes.shared: The program manager prepares a monthly match schedule and backup pack that the grantor's monitor receives with the reimbursement invoice.

buildPlan.title: One award, one schedule
buildPlan.delivers: Sign in, create an award with its match requirement and period, import a POINT hours CSV, and see the month's matched hours and value at one rate.
buildPlan.acceptance: A signed-in user imports a 50-row sample POINT export and the schedule total equals a hand-worked figure; deployed.

buildPlan.title: Rate table with its basis
buildPlan.delivers: Define roles with an hourly rate and the documented basis for it (the organisation's pay for similar work, a wage source), and value each entry by role.
buildPlan.acceptance: Changing a role's rate revalues its entries; a rate with no basis recorded cannot be used in a schedule.

buildPlan.title: Allocation and the double-count lock
buildPlan.delivers: Allocate approved entries to one award; an entry already allocated cannot be counted for another award; caps per award period.
buildPlan.acceptance: A test that allocates one entry to two awards is refused; an allocation past the period cap is flagged and kept out of the schedule.

buildPlan.title: Monthly schedule and backup pack
buildPlan.delivers: Download a monthly match schedule per award (CSV and PDF) and a backup pack listing each entry's volunteer, date, hours, role, rate, basis, source file and import time.
buildPlan.acceptance: For a seeded month the schedule total equals the sum of allocated entries and the PDF opens with every entry listed.

buildPlan.title: Other imports and reminders
buildPlan.delivers: Map the columns of a Golden or SignUpGenius export or any sheet once and reuse the mapping; a reminder email before each invoice date.
buildPlan.acceptance: A mapped sample sheet imports with no lost rows; a scheduled run sends exactly one reminder for a seeded award.

buildPlan.title: Polish
buildPlan.delivers: A plain-language guide for program managers, phone layout, keyboard and screen-reader pass, an audit-log view and a walkthrough test.
buildPlan.acceptance: A walkthrough test runs sign-in to schedule export; axe reports no serious issues.

ideas.summary: For small non-profits that meet a grant's match with volunteer time: turns hours from a free volunteer tool into a monthly match schedule per award, valued at documented rates and never counted twice.

public.summary: Turn your volunteers' hours into a monthly match schedule for each grant, ready to send with your invoice.
public.problem: Your grant asks you to match it, and volunteer time can count, but only if every hour is documented, valued fairly and claimed for one grant only. Your hours sit in a volunteer app or a spreadsheet, so each month you rebuild the match by hand and hope nothing is counted twice.
public.forWhom: Program managers and finance leads at small non-profits whose grants require a volunteer or in-kind match.
benefits: A monthly match schedule for each grant, ready to attach
Every hour valued at a rate you can explain
No hour counted for two grants
A backup pack that answers a monitor's questions
A reminder before each invoice is due

ideas.problemStatement: Volunteer hours sit in POINT, Golden, SignUpGenius or a spreadsheet, but a grant's match must be verifiable in the records, counted for no other federal award, and valued at rates consistent with pay for similar work; small non-profits rebuild that schedule by hand each month, and weak records can turn an in-kind match into a cash match or a smaller award.
ideas.description: A companion to the free volunteer tool the organisation already uses. The program manager imports approved hours as CSV, sets up each match-requiring award with its period and required match, and keeps a role rate table where every rate carries its documented basis. Entries are allocated to exactly one award and locked against the others, with caps per period, and the app produces a monthly match schedule per award plus a backup pack listing every hour behind it. A scheduled reminder goes out before each invoice date. It prepares the schedule; the organisation still certifies it.
ideas.targetCustomer: Program managers and grants or finance leads at small non-profits holding one or more grants that require a cost-share or in-kind match, such as state service commission Volunteer Generation Fund subgrantees, AmeriCorps programs and state pass-through grants.
ideas.buyer: The organisation, from its program or admin budget; Florida's 2026-27 Volunteer Generation Fund notice lists volunteer management software as an allowable cost, so the grant itself may pay.
ideas.whyNow: Florida's 2026-27 Volunteer Generation Fund notice (August 2026) requires a 50% cash or in-kind match with monthly invoices and the same documentation for the match; Zeffy has no hour tracking and Givebutter's volunteer request has been open since 2022; the free tools that track hours (POINT, Golden, VolunteerBadge) value them at one rate and do not allocate them to awards.

ideas.revenueSketch: Estimate: 100 organisations with two or more match-requiring awards at $190 a year = $19,000 a year; the count of such organisations is an assumption, not a measured figure.
ideas.distribution: First 10: search content and a small search-ad test on match-documentation terms ('volunteer in-kind match', 'value volunteer hours grant match'), landing on a free match calculator; later a listing request through Givebutter's partner page (https://givebutter.com/partner; listing rules unknown: check before applying). r/nonprofit: rule unknown, check before posting (the rules page returned 403). validationTest.method: A landing page, 'Monthly in-kind match schedules for volunteer hours', with a free match calculator and a price button ($19 a month or $190 a year) leading to a waitlist that asks for the organisation and the grant; a 14-day search-ad test on match-documentation terms; no outreach, no contact with posters and no posts in evidence threads.

Privacy: volunteer names, emails and hours need a privacy notice and deletion on request; launch US-only to avoid GDPR at first.
Minors: no student hour letters and no self-logging, so the app holds no minors' accounts; coordinators import hours only.
Grant records: an append-only audit log and exports for the organisation's files.

risks.mitigation: Require a documented basis for every rate and label the output as prepared for the organisation's review.

risks.mitigation: Aim at every grant type that takes in-kind match, and price for organisations holding two or more awards.

scoreRationale.pain: Recent complaints ask for hour tracking (https://feedback.zeffy.com/feature-requests/p/volunteer-time-management, 2026-10-22) and the match rule has consequences (https://www.dcjs.virginia.gov/node/5508), but no complaint about documenting match itself was found, so 3.
scoreRationale.willingnessToPay: One paid app sells the in-kind value of volunteer time (Volunteer Ledger, https://apps.apple.com/app/id6824345952), and Florida allows software as a grant cost (https://www.volunteerflorida.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/VGF-2026-NOFO.pdf); VolunteerBadge's free in-kind value holds it at 3.
scoreRationale.reachability: Self-serve search only; no community whose promotion rule could be read, and state commissions would be partnerships (https://www.volunteerflorida.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/VGF-2026-NOFO.pdf).
scoreRationale.competitiveGap: VolunteerBadge gives approval, an audit trail, in-kind value and grant reports free (https://www.volunteerbadge.com/pricing) and Track It Forward reports by a grant field (https://help.trackitforward.com/doc/reports-faq); only the rate basis, the one-award lock, caps and the monthly schedule are left.
scoreRationale.feasibility: CSV import of a documented export (https://support.pointapp.org/knowledge/how-can-i-export-a-volunteers-hours-report-as-an-admin), rate tables, allocation, PDF, a scheduled email: about 6 build days once self-logging and API imports are dropped.
scoreRationale.complianceBurden: Volunteer names and hours only, no minors' accounts and no institutional contract; the grantee certifies the match (https://www.ecfr.gov/api/renderer/v1/content/enhanced/current/title-2?part=200&section=200.306).

review.findings: Research kept the idea but narrowed it: POINT and Golden already track hours free, POINT syncs hours into Givebutter nightly, Zeffy closed its volunteer option, and no free product allocates hours to one award at 2 CFR 200.306 rates. The adversarial reviewer cut it from 19 to 18 (competitiveGap 3 to 2) after finding VolunteerBadge's free plan with approval, an audit trail, in-kind match value and grant reports; it found that every complaint asks for hour tracking, not match, that the AmeriCorps inspector general's $1 million figure covers all kinds of match, that Givebutter's and Zeffy's APIs carry no hours (so imports are CSV only), and that Florida allows software as a grant cost. It re-scoped the idea to a match schedule and allocation companion for organisations holding two or more match-requiring awards, dropped self-logging, API imports and student letters, and asked for a name unlike Volunteer Ledger's.

missing: pain 3 is below 4: the complaints ask for hour tracking, which free tools give; no dated complaint about documenting a volunteer match was found
gateGap.closedBy: The landing-page and search-ad test: 8 sign-ups that name a match-requiring grant and 3% price-button clicks would show willingness to pay; a dated complaint about a questioned or rejected volunteer match would lift pain to 4.

ideas.title: Back Issue Article Index for Society Journals

notes.stateful: The editor keeps the society's issues, the articles found in each with their page spans, titles and authors, and every correction, and adds each new issue.
notes.connected: Reads the society's own born-digital issue PDFs and links each search result to the society's own copy at #page=N; exports CSV and JSON citations the society can send to PERSI or a philatelic library.
notes.engine: Proposes article boundaries from the contents page and headings, reassembles articles that continue on a later page, and extracts title, author and section.
notes.shared: The editor builds and corrects the index; members and the public search the embedded article-level page.

buildPlan.title: One issue, one index
buildPlan.delivers: Sign in, upload one text-layer issue PDF, see its articles proposed from the contents page with title, author and page span, and search them.
buildPlan.acceptance: On a sample 40-page issue, every article on the contents page appears with the right first page; a search for an author returns that article; deployed.

buildPlan.title: Corrections and jumps
buildPlan.delivers: Correct, split or merge proposed articles in a list view, and join an article that continues on a later page.
buildPlan.acceptance: A seeded 'continued on page 10' article comes back as one result spanning both page ranges; corrections survive sign-out and sign-in.

buildPlan.title: Backfile upload
buildPlan.delivers: Upload a batch of past issues, process them in the background within a capped model budget per issue, and review them one by one.
buildPlan.acceptance: A 20-issue batch processes with no lost issue and the model spend per issue stays under the set cap.

buildPlan.title: Embeddable search page
buildPlan.delivers: A public article-level search page with filters for author, year and section, linking to the society's own PDFs at the right page, embeddable in any website.
buildPlan.acceptance: The page embeds in a test WordPress page and a plain HTML page; each result opens the society's PDF at the article's first page.

ideas.summary: For volunteer editors of philatelic, natural-history and other small societies: turns decades of back-issue PDFs into an article-level index members can search, which the society keeps and can export.

public.summary: Turn your society's back issues into a searchable index of every article, by title, author and year.
public.problem: Your society has published its journal for decades, but a member searching the archive gets whole issues back, if anything. Volunteers have tried to list every article by hand, it takes many hours, and articles that continue on a later page get lost.
public.forWhom: Volunteer editors, librarians and webmasters of small societies that publish a journal or newsletter.
benefits: Every article findable by title, author, year and section
Articles that continue on a later page come back whole
A search page you can put on your own website
An index you keep and can take with you

ideas.problemStatement: Small societies keep decades of journal issues as PDFs that are searchable only by issue; volunteers split issues into articles and build indexes by hand, unreliably and over many hours, and articles that jump pages are lost.
ideas.description: The editor uploads issue PDFs that already carry text. The app proposes each issue's articles from its contents page and headings, with title, author, section and page span, and joins articles that continue on a later page; the editor corrects them in a list. A public article-level search page links each result to the society's own PDF at the right page and embeds in any website, so the app hosts no page images. The whole index exports as CSV, JSON, a citation list and a static HTML copy. Scanned issues, members-only pages and comments are left out of the first version.
ideas.targetCustomer: Volunteer editors, librarians and webmasters of small philatelic, natural-history and similar societies with about 50 to 500 back issues as text-layer PDFs; genealogy and local-history societies come second, since PERSI already indexes many of their periodicals.
ideas.buyer: The society, from its publications or website budget, approved by its board or committee.
ideas.whyNow: Societies are building article indexes by hand right now (a Scottish family history society launched one on 2026-05-08 with 100 issues still to list; a philatelic society finished one in 2026), and a stamp club posted a USD 3,000 to 5,000 job for article-level search on 2026-11-22.

problemEvidence.author: poster A
problemEvidence.summary: A stamp club officer posts a fixed USD 3,000 to 5,000 job (about 300 bids) for article-level search of a quarterly journal, including articles across non-adjacent pages, by author, advertiser and year; a volunteer splits issues by hand, 'which has not been reliable'. The club wants to own the code, which reads as a custom build.

problemEvidence.author: poster B
problemEvidence.summary: A family history society launches a hand-built index of over 1,000 magazine articles and says that, 'with over 100 issues to create listings for, that will take time'.

problemEvidence.author: poster C
problemEvidence.summary: A philatelic society's site admin announces a topic index for 1937 to 2022 that a member 'spent many hours reading the back issues' to build; its own issue-level search warns that long articles were 'broken up and spread across issues and even years' (https://militaryphs.org/back-issues-search.html).

competitors.name: PERSI (Periodical Source Index)
competitors.gap: Over 3.2 million subject citations to articles in genealogy and local-history periodicals, but citations only, not full text, and the society cannot embed or control it.

competitors.name: APRL Philatelic Union Catalog
competitors.gap: Article records for philatelic periodicals, but in a library catalog, not on the society's own site with full-text search.

competitors.name: Archive in a Box
competitors.gap: PDF upload, page-level OCR and multi-page records, but no article splitting, no export and everything public.

competitors.name: WebEquipe PDF Search for WordPress
competitors.gap: One result per PDF, no articles and no author index.

competitors.name: Internet Archive full-text search
competitors.gap: Finds pages, not articles, and only for issues the society is willing to make public there.

keyFeatures: Articles proposed from each issue's contents page and headings
Continued-on articles joined into one result
Correction list for the volunteer editor
Embeddable article-level search linking to the society's own PDFs
Full export: CSV, JSON, citations and a static copy

outOfScope: OCR of scanned issues (a later add-on priced per page)
members-only pages tied to the society's membership system

ideas.techStack: React + Vite, in-browser PDF text extraction, the shared Supabase project for sign-in and the index, the LLM gateway with a capped budget per issue for article proposals.

pricing.model: A one-time backfile fee plus a small yearly fee per society
pricing.pricePoint: $99 to index a backfile of up to 300 issues, then $49 a year
pricing.rationale: Far below the USD 3,000 to 5,000 custom-build quote and the publishers' tools, near Omeka.net's $35 to $75 plans; the reviewer advised against bundling a large backfile into one yearly price because of the model cost per page.

ideas.revenueSketch: Estimate: 60 societies a year at $99 plus $49 a year = about $8,900 in the first year; the number of societies is an assumption, not a measured figure.
ideas.distribution: First 10: a how-to article on indexing a society journal for The Philatelic Communicator of the American Philatelic Society's Writers Unit #30, whose journal says 'Manuscripts are welcomed on subjects of interest to writers, editors, and publishers of all forms of philatelic literature' (https://wu30.org/tpc/2025/20251t.pdf); advertising there: rule unknown, check before submitting. Second, a free WordPress.org plugin that embeds the search page: the directory allows a plugin that interfaces with an external service 'even for paid services' but forbids features locked behind payment and contacting servers without consent (https://developer.wordpress.org/plugins/wordpress-org/detailed-plugin-guidelines/). Never bid on, reply to or contact the evidence job's poster or the societies in the evidence.

validationTest.method: A landing page, 'An index of every article in your society's back issues', with a demo built from public-domain issues, a waitlist that asks for the society and its number of issues, and a '$99 backfile' price button; a two-week search-ad test on 'index society journal', 'searchable newsletter archive' and 'digitize back issues'; re-run the freelancer.com searches weekly for 4 weeks to count new paid jobs; no outreach.
validationTest.successCriteria: At least 10 waitlist sign-ups that name a society, 3 price-button clicks, and one more paid job for the same task within 4 weeks.
validationTest.cost: About $100 to $150 in ads, a domain and one build day for the demo.

ideas.moat: Article boundaries and continued-on joins tuned on many societies' layouts, and each society's corrected index, are hard to copy quickly; the full export keeps trust but means no lock-in.
compliance: Copyright: contributors' and advertisers' rights to old issues rest with the society; terms say so and a takedown process removes an article from the index.
Privacy: editor accounts hold names and emails; genealogy newsletters name living people, so an index of names stays off by default.
No students' or minors' records and no institutional contract.

risks.risk: The one paid buyer wants a custom build it owns, not a subscription.
risks.mitigation: Full export and a static copy, and the price-button test before building.

risks.risk: Free indexes (PERSI, APRL) already serve genealogy, local-history and philatelic subject search.
risks.mitigation: Sell full-text article search on the society's own site, and export citations to those indexes rather than compete with them.

risks.risk: Article proposals go wrong on unusual layouts.
risks.mitigation: Born-digital PDFs only at first, every proposal corrected by the editor, and model reading of layouts is checked, since 'fluent output is not proof of accuracy' (https://islam.zmo.de/s/westafrica/page/ocr).
A capped budget per issue through the gateway and a one-time backfile fee.

scoreRationale.pain: One complaint inside a paid job (https://www.freelancer.com/projects/wordpress/Build-Searchable-Journal-Archive, manual splitting 'has not been reliable') and hand-built indexes at two societies (https://bordersfhs.org.uk/magazine-article-index-now-live/, https://militaryphs.org/blog/2026/03/12/master-index-of-the-mphs-bulletin-now-available/), which are workarounds more than complaints, so 3.
scoreRationale.willingnessToPay: One dated paid job at USD 3,000 to 5,000 for this task (https://www.freelancer.com/projects/wordpress/Build-Searchable-Journal-Archive), though for a custom build the club will own.
scoreRationale.reachability: A self-serve channel through the APS Writers Unit #30 journal, which welcomes submissions on publishing philatelic literature (https://wu30.org/tpc/2025/20251t.pdf), and the WordPress plugin directory (https://developer.wordpress.org/plugins/wordpress-org/detailed-plugin-guidelines/).
scoreRationale.competitiveGap: PERSI (https://www.genealogycenter.info/persi/) and APRL (https://stamps.org/Services/Library/Philatelic-Union-Catalog-Details) already give free article citations for genealogy, local-history and philatelic periodicals; only full-text article search on the society's own site is left.
scoreRationale.feasibility: Born-digital PDFs only, a list view for corrections, links to the society's own PDFs instead of hosted page images: 6 to 7 build days; scans and member gating would push it past 7 (https://islam.zmo.de/s/westafrica/page/ocr).
scoreRationale.complianceBurden: Contributor copyright and a takedown process; no students' records and no institutional contract (https://www.archiveinabox.com/why-us.php shows a free host that blocks downloads for the same reason).

review.findings: Research confirmed the stamp club's job (USD 3,000 to 5,000, posted about 2026-11-22) and found no small-society tool that splits issues into articles and follows continued-on pages; it found the job was the only paid one in about 90 days of freelancer.com searches. The adversarial reviewer cut the researched version from 19 to 17 (competitiveGap 3 to 2, feasibility 3 to 2): PERSI and APRL's catalog already give free article citations for genealogy, local-history and philatelic periodicals; the only buyer wants to own a much larger custom build; the three MPHS pages are one society and a finished workaround, not complaints, and one quote was on a different page; scans, page images and member gating exceed 7 days; and OCR costs per page make a bundled backfile unprofitable. It added a new independent society building its index by hand (2026-05-08) and re-scoped the idea to born-digital PDFs with a list-view editor, links to the society's own PDFs and a full export, which it expected to raise feasibility to 3 or 4; this file takes 3, for a total of 18.

missing: pain 3 is below 4: one complaint inside a paid job, and societies' hand-built indexes are workarounds
willingnessToPay rests on one paid job, and it is for a custom build
gateGap.closedBy: The landing-page and price-button test: 10 sign-ups naming a society and 3 clicks on the $99 backfile button would show that societies buy a product rather than a build; a second paid job within 4 weeks would make the spend more than one club's.

ideas.title: Zeffy Payout Journals for Xero

notes.stateful: The treasurer keeps saved rules from campaign, rate and fund to Xero account codes and tracking categories, and a history of payout totals.
notes.connected: Reads Zeffy's per-payout and itemised payments exports and writes a Xero manual-journal import file, both the organisation's own files.
notes.engine: Groups payments by payout, checks the sum against the payout amount, takes refunds from the payout report, and builds a balanced journal against a Zeffy clearing account.
notes.shared: A one-page payout summary the treasurer makes and the board receives.

ideas.summary: For Zeffy organisations that keep their books in Xero: turns each Zeffy payout into a ready-to-import Xero journal, coded by campaign and fund.

public.summary: Turn each Zeffy payout into a Xero journal you can import, already split by campaign and fund.
public.problem: Zeffy connects to QuickBooks but not to Xero, so every payout that lands in your bank has to be rebuilt by hand from two exports. You split it by campaign, find the refunds, and type it into Xero again each week or month.
public.forWhom: Volunteer treasurers and bookkeepers of charities, clubs and school groups that take money through Zeffy and keep their books in Xero.
benefits: Each payout matched to the payments inside it
Income coded to your accounts and tracking categories
A one-page payout summary for the board

ideas.problemStatement: Zeffy connects natively only to QuickBooks Online; a treasurer who keeps the books in Xero rebuilds each payout by hand from the payout export and the itemised payments export, splitting it by campaign and fund and adding refunds, which appear only in the payout report.
ideas.description: The treasurer uploads Zeffy's per-payout export and the itemised payments export; the app maps columns by header, groups payments by payout and checks the total against the payout amount. Saved rules map each campaign, rate and fund to a Xero account code and up to two tracking categories, and refunds are taken from the payout report. It produces a balanced Xero manual-journal import against a Zeffy clearing account (Xero journals cannot post to a bank account), with a one-time guide to the bank rule that codes each Zeffy deposit to that clearing account, and a one-page payout summary for the board. Files are parsed in the browser; only rules and payout totals are saved.
ideas.targetCustomer: Volunteer treasurers and part-time bookkeepers of small charities, clubs and school groups that take money through Zeffy (US, Canada, UK, Ireland, Australia) and keep their books in Xero.
ideas.buyer: The organisation, from its admin budget; these buyers are price-sensitive, having chosen Zeffy because it is free and Xero because it is cheaper.
ideas.whyNow: Zeffy launched in the UK, Australia and Ireland, where Xero is common, and says it connects natively only to QuickBooks (https://www.zeffy.com/en-au/integration/api); its Xero request has had comments every few weeks since August 2026 with no staff reply, while its 2026-11-17 release made per-payout exports usable for this.

problemEvidence.author: poster A
problemEvidence.summary: Open request for a Xero integration (opened 2026-05-18, 10 votes, no staff reply); distinct accounts commented on 2026-08-28, 09-15, 09-17, 10-26, 11-18 and about 11-21, mostly '+1'; the 2026-09-15 commenter chose Xero because it is cheaper and has a non-profit discount.

problemEvidence.author: poster B
problemEvidence.summary: A user who imports Zeffy reports into Xero says ticket and added donation on one line force manual adjustment in Xero; 4 votes; Zeffy marked it complete on 2026-10-01.

problemEvidence.author: poster C
problemEvidence.summary: A service club asks on Xero's ideas forum for Zeffy payouts mapped to accounts, campaign and fund; 2 votes, no reply.

competitors.name: Zeffy's QuickBooks Online sync
competitors.gap: QuickBooks only; nothing for organisations on Xero.

competitors.name: Zeffy's own payout exports
competitors.gap: Since 2026-11-17 a payout shows its payments by campaign, but it is still a spreadsheet with no mapping to ledger accounts; a treasurer's guide puts the manual job at 20 to 30 minutes a month.

competitors.name: Zapier Zeffy app
competitors.price: Free plan; paid plans for multi-step Zaps
competitors.gap: Payment and contact triggers only, no payout trigger, so it cannot reconcile a payout.

competitors.name: MoneyMinder
competitors.gap: Integrates Zeffy since 2026-07-22 but replaces the ledger; no help to an organisation that keeps its books in Xero.

competitors.name: Stripe-based tools (Xero's Stripe feed, Synder, A2X)
competitors.gap: Zeffy does not let organisations connect their own Stripe account, so tools that read Stripe payouts do not apply.

keyFeatures: Payout grouping with a total check
Saved rules from campaign, rate and fund to account codes and tracking
Refunds taken from the payout report
Balanced Xero journal against a clearing account
One-page payout summary for the board

outOfScope: Xero API connection (more than 5 organisations needs a paid Xero developer tier)
Zeffy API (it has no payout object)

ideas.techStack: React + Vite with in-browser CSV parsing, the shared Supabase project for sign-in and saved rules; no Xero or Zeffy API.

pricing.model: Per organisation, first three payouts free
pricing.rationale: Far below MoneyMinder ($299 a year) and Zapier's paid plans, because these buyers chose Zeffy for being free; three free payouts rather than one a month, since an organisation paid monthly would otherwise never pay.

ideas.revenueSketch: Estimate: 150 Zeffy organisations on Xero at $49 a year = $7,350 a year; the number of such organisations is unknown and this is an assumption.
ideas.distribution: First 10: a landing page built for 'zeffy xero' searches and a small search-ad test in the UK, Ireland, Australia, New Zealand, Canada and the US; a later application to Zeffy's Experts directory (https://www.zeffy.com/home/affiliate-expert, rule unknown: check before applying). Zeffy's community guidelines say 'Off-topic promotion or spam doesn't belong here' (https://community.zeffy.com/community-guidelines): not a channel. Xero Community forum: rule unknown, check before posting. Never post on Zeffy's feature board or Xero's ideas forum, which hold the evidence.

validationTest.method: A landing page with a demo on a synthetic payout file, a '$49 a year' price button and a waitlist; search ads on 'zeffy xero', 'zeffy xero integration', 'zeffy accounting export' and 'zeffy payout report' for 3 weeks in the six countries; no outreach and no posts in evidence threads.
validationTest.successCriteria: At least 8 waitlist sign-ups and 3 price-button clicks in 3 weeks; stop if fewer than 3 sign-ups, if the ads cannot serve for lack of search volume, or if Zeffy announces a Xero sync.
validationTest.cost: About $150 in ads, a domain and one build day.

ideas.moat: Little: header mapping across Zeffy's changing exports, refund handling and the clearing-account pattern are small know-how; Zeffy could close the gap with a native Xero sync.
compliance: Privacy: donor names, addresses and tributes are parsed in the browser and not stored; only rules and payout totals are saved (UK GDPR, the Australian Privacy Act, PIPEDA).
Minors: custom answers may hold children's names in school and youth groups, so those columns are dropped on import.
Accounting: the output is a journal for the treasurer to review and import; the app gives no Gift Aid or tax opinion.

risks.risk: Zeffy ships a native Xero sync.
risks.mitigation: Build small and stop on any Zeffy announcement of Xero.

risks.risk: A tiny market: about ten voters on the Xero request.
risks.mitigation: Run the search-ad test before building.

risks.risk: Zeffy's export columns change and vary by user.
risks.mitigation: Map columns by header and keep test fixtures from the documented exports.

risks.risk: The manual job is small (20 to 30 minutes a month).
risks.mitigation: Price low and sell the board summary and the caught refunds, not the time saved alone.

scoreRationale.pain: About ten '+1' comments (https://feedback.zeffy.com/feature-requests/p/xero-integration), Zeffy fixed the ticket and donation split on 2026-10-01 (https://feedback.zeffy.com/feature-requests/p/break-out-ticket-amount-and-additional-donation-amount-on-separate-line-items-in), and a treasurer's guide puts the job at 20 to 30 minutes a month (https://www.zeffy.com/blog/understanding-zeffy-payouts-webinar-recap).
scoreRationale.willingnessToPay: No payment evidence from Xero users, and the 2026-09-15 commenter chose Xero to save money (https://feedback.zeffy.com/feature-requests/p/xero-integration).
scoreRationale.reachability: No App Store listing without the Xero API and no community that allows promotion; search intent only (https://xero.uservoice.com/forums/28866-new-integrations/suggestions/51241744-zeffy-integration-payments-mapped-to-accounts-ca).
scoreRationale.competitiveGap: No native, Zapier or Stripe-based path for Xero users (https://www.zeffy.com/en-au/integration/api, https://support.zeffy.com/what-is-stripe-f1fsz), but Zeffy's own exports keep improving (https://www.zeffy.com/home/releases).
scoreRationale.feasibility: CSV in, Xero journal CSV out against a clearing account, since Xero journals cannot post to a bank account (https://productideas.xero.com/forums/967133-reports-tax/suggestions/47749109-manual-journals-ability-to-post-journal-entries): 4 to 5 build days.
scoreRationale.complianceBurden: Parsed in the browser with only rules and totals stored (https://www.zeffy.com/blog/how-to-reconcile-zeffy-payouts).

review.findings: Research ended the original QuickBooks-facing payout reconciler: Zeffy shipped per-payout exports on 2026-11-17 and an itemised QuickBooks sync on 2026-11-19, and MoneyMinder integrates Zeffy since 2026-07-22. It re-scoped the idea to Zeffy organisations on Xero, which have no path. The adversarial reviewer cut it from 19 to 17 (pain 3 to 2, willingnessToPay 3 to 2): the Xero request is ten '+1's with no payment evidence, Zeffy fixed the ticket and donation split upstream, a treasurer's guide on Zeffy's blog puts the manual job at 20 to 30 minutes a month, the MoneyMinder and QuickBooks posts are other customers, and Xero manual journals cannot post to a bank account, so the journal must use a clearing account and a bank rule. It found no free or cheap product for Xero users, since Zeffy does not let organisations connect their own Stripe account, and changed the free tier to three payouts.

missing: pain 2 is below 4: the complaints are short '+1's and the manual job takes 20 to 30 minutes a month
willingnessToPay 2 is below 3: no payment evidence from Zeffy organisations on Xero
gateGap.closedBy: The search-ad test: 8 waitlist sign-ups and 3 clicks on the $49 price button in 3 weeks would lift willingnessToPay to 3; dated complaints from Xero treasurers about the time payouts take would lift pain.

rejectedCandidates.title: Term Report Builder for Small Lesson Schools
rejectedCandidates.reason: Research ended it: autoCrat, a free Google Sheets add-on with 83M+ installs, fills a branded template, makes one PDF per student and emails it with a log; Khanmigo writes report comments free; Teach 'n Go already makes report-card PDFs and has a custom template in Testing; the main complaints date from March 2024.

rejectedCandidates.title: Renewal Rebook Desk for Small First-Aid Training Providers
rejectedCandidates.reason: Research ended it: CPR Enroll, Hovn ($50 a month), Enrollware, Arlo and accessplanit already send expiry reminders with rebooking links; WSIB's 2026-06-22 change sets no record duty on providers; no complaint and no paid job.

rejectedCandidates.title: Makeup Slot Offers for Swim and Music Schools
rejectedCandidates.reason: Research ended it: TutorBird and My Music Staff ($16.95 a month) track and expire make-up credits with self-booking, iClassPro has make-up tokens on every plan and automatic waitlist offers, and Zenamu books waitlisted credit holders; no owner complaint and no paid job.

rejectedCandidates.title: Staff Registry Check Log for New York Lesson Studios
rejectedCandidates.reason: Research ended it: bill S5257-C passed both houses on 2026-05-29 but shows no governor action, its text sets no record-keeping duty, the searches are free, and Jackrabbit already tracks staff certifications with 60-month expiry and 30-day alerts. Worth a look again only if it is signed.

rejectedCandidates.title: Class Roster, Waitlist and Waiver for Shopify Shops That Teach
rejectedCandidates.reason: Research ended it: Still Works Class Booking (free for 4 dates a month, $19 unlimited) gives sessions, seats, waitlist, roster and check-in from one product, esigned ($9 a month) chases unsigned waivers, and at least six class or ticket apps launched since May 2026.

rejectedCandidates.title: Course Platform Exit Kit for Small Course Businesses
rejectedCandidates.reason: Research ended it: Podia, FreshLearn, Circle and Teachable migrate courses and students free; six freelancer.com queries found no paid job to move a course off Kajabi, Thinkific or Teachable; recent complaints are about price, not migration work.

rejectedCandidates.title: Certificates and Attendance Records for Small Continuing-Education Providers
rejectedCandidates.reason: Research ended it: CE-Go (free account, from $5 per participant) is built for CE providers, Zoom shipped its own certificates in February 2026, and Certifier's free plan has a Zoom attendance threshold; the only complaints date from 2023 and 2024.

rejectedCandidates.title: Children Not in School Records for Tutors and Tuition Centres (England)
rejectedCandidates.reason: Research ended it: the provider duty has no start date (DfE consultation 2026-11-12 to 2027-02-03, response in spring 2027), the proposed six-hours-a-week threshold leaves out most tutors, and the DfE expects replies by email or letter at 15 minutes per student a year.

rejectedCandidates.title: COPPA Yearly Program Kit for Small Kids' Online Class Businesses
rejectedCandidates.reason: Research ended it: the FTC's FAQ says COPPA covers data collected online from children, not from parents, so parent-registered live classes are at best a grey zone; the FTC's free six-step plan already explains the written program and retention policy sized to the operator; no complaint and no paid job.

rejectedCandidates.title: Tutoring Business Back Office (intake, session log, invoices, progress)
rejectedCandidates.reason: Not given its own researcher: today's makeup-slot and practice-log research read TutorBird and My Music Staff at $16.95 a month, which cover scheduling, invoicing, credits and logs for the same customer; TPT spend is $2 binders and unrated kits.

rejectedCandidates.title: Video Host Exit Kit for Course Creators Leaving Vimeo
rejectedCandidates.reason: Research ended it: Livid's free exporter and WordPress plugin, bunny.net's free vimeo2bunny, Gumlet's ID-keeping import with free Better Search Replace, and Swarmify ($19 a month) move videos and swap embeds; Kajabi, Teachable and Thinkific host video natively; no complaint from a course creator.

rejectedCandidates.title: SCORM Packages for Small Course Sellers Who Sell to Companies
rejectedCandidates.reason: Research ended it: the two freelance jobs were a creator's new course for their own site and a company's own L&D team, not this customer; free converters package video and PDF as SCORM, and SCORM Cloud Dispatch ($99 a month) and LearnKey ($179 a month) sell licence control.

rejectedCandidates.title: Evidence Pack for Apprenticeship Unit Providers (England)

runNotes.caveats: Only one idea ships today, and it is provisional. Twenty-four candidates were scored (23 new and the one watchlist entry, re-researched); none came near the gate of 22. Three fell to rejection rules. Sixteen went to researchers, in four rounds down the ranked list, and research ended fifteen of them because an incumbent already does the same job for the same customer, often free or for about $17 a month (TutorBird and My Music Staff, iClassPro, autoCrat, CE-Go and Zoom's own certificates, Still Works, free course migrations, Aptem, OneFile and Bud for apprenticeship units, Livid and Gumlet for Vimeo moves, Homeschool Fox, PracticeAlly), or because the mandate has no start date or does not reach the buyer (New York S5257-C unsigned; England's Children Not in School provider duty in consultation; COPPA and parent-registered classes); three more were closed with pages already read today (tutoring back office, Florida coach screening, tutor reputation records), and three Teach 'n Go requests were merged into one candidate. Only the Zeffy waiver entry survived research, and its one adversarial review rescored it from 18 to 16. The run ran out of candidates after 1 review, so it ships fewer than 3 ideas and fewer than 10 reviews were held. No idea has a small-business buyer: the buyer of idea 1 is a small nonprofit, camp, club or parent group on Zeffy, which is free for nonprofits; no small-business candidate survived research. Idea 1 is substantial and Multi-week with a build plan. The selection constraint of one Weekend MVP and one Multi-week idea does not apply with one idea. The watchlist is empty: the only entry (first seen 2026-11-21) ships today as idea 1, and no other candidate scored 19 or more. Extra run (random sources A3 A11 B6 C6 B9): run on the owner's direction recorded by PManager (ledger 2026-11-25T07:27Z, 'more education or non-profit like projects'), so every candidate was an education or non-profit idea and the random sources were searched with that lens, with supplementary searches on A2 (the Blackbaud K-12 community), A5, A12, A16 (the Zeffy and Givebutter boards), B1 and B11; it ran at 23:28 Los Angeles time on 24 November, so it adds to this file. It added ideas 2, 3 and 4, all provisional: Volunteer Match Schedules for Grants (18), Back Issue Article Index for Society Journals (18) and Zeffy Payout Journals for Xero (17). Fifteen candidates were scored; three had a small-business buyer (private schools, coaching institutes, private academies) and none of them reached research, so the day still has no small-business idea. Eight candidates were researched (four ended there) and four were reviewed (three survived, all rescored down; one fell below the floor). Ideas 2 and 3 are substantial and Multi-week with build plans; idea 4 is the Weekend MVP. The watchlist stays empty: no unshipped candidate scored 19 or more after research.
